issues.failure_explanation: The step bounds the local error norm by |B(w,w)| 'using the coercivity ... of the bilinear form'. For divergence-free b, B(.,.)_{D*} is coercive only on H^1_{D,0}(D*), i.e. for functions that also vanish on the interior boundary (as the paper's own definition of the local test space shows: u = 0 on (boundary(D*)∩Γ_D) ∪ (boundary(D*)∩Ω)). The function w = u^e|_{D*} − u^p_j does not lie in this class: u^p_j vanishes on boundary(D*)∩Ω but u^e does not, so the convective flux term −(1/2)∫_{boundary(D*)∩Ω} w^2 (b·n) is uncontrolled and B(w,w) can be smaller than ||w||_a^2. Likewise, the subsequent continuity estimate with constant (1 + C_{D*_j}H*_j a_min^{-1}||b||_∞) implicitly uses a Poincaré inequality for w on D*_j, which fails for oversampling domains not touching Γ_D. Finally, the stated constant (1 + C Pe_H)^2 cannot absorb the global operator norm C_B entering Theorem th:msgfem:global, which is governed by the global (not subdomain) Péclet scale.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the coercivity step by a contained well-posedness argument for the local subproblem: from the harmonicity orthogonality B(u^e - u^p_j, u^p_j)_{D*_j} = 0 and the global weak equation one gets F_{D*}(xi) = B(u^e, xi)_{D*}, whence a bound of the form ||u^e - u^p_j||_{a,D*} <= C(1 + Pe_{H*_j}) ||u^e||_{a,D*} follows from continuity/coercivity on H^1_{D,0}(D*); restate the global simplification with the constant actually delivered by Theorem th:msgfem:global (including the global-continuity contribution).
issues.overall_effect: The quasi-optimal bound (eq:msgfem:global:coercive) with its explicit constant is not established; since Theorem th:msgfem:iteration derives the existence of coarse spaces with any prescribed contraction factor from this corollary, that convergence guarantee is also left unsupported.
issues.title: Coercivity invoked outside its valid class in the proof of Corollary cor:added-1
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained, nontrivial re-derivation of one estimate using tools the paper already assumes (well-posedness of subdomain problems, continuity of B); no new proof architecture is needed and a comparable quasi-optimality statement with a correspondingly adjusted constant survives.

issues.failure_explanation: Estimate (msgfem:iteration:1) bounds ||u^e - G u^e|| at the single input u^e; an operator-norm bound ||(I-G)v|| <= vartheta ||v|| for all v cannot be inferred from it. Establishing such a bound requires rerunning the local approximation theory (Caccioppoli inequality, weak approximation property, eigenfunction expansion in the B-harmonic space) with v replaced by an arbitrary error function. All of these ingredients are stated only for the class H_B(D*_j) of functions vanishing on the Dirichlet part of the boundary, and the iterated errors (I-G)^k(u^{(0)} - u^e) for general u^{(0)} in H^1(Omega) do not belong to that class; the paper neither proves the operator bound nor shows the relevant function class is invariant under I - G. The displayed estimate is also written in the oversampling-domain norm while the theorem's contraction claim is in the global norm.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the statement to initial guesses whose errors lie in the Dirichlet trace class covered by the local theory, and supply the missing operator-norm step by applying Theorems th:msgfem:local and th:msgfem:global (with Corollary cor:added-1) to an arbitrary such error function rather than only to u^e; alternatively reformulate the iteration on the homogeneous correction problem, as the discrete iteration (eq:msgfem:iteration:discrete) effectively does, and prove contraction there.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's main theoretical convergence guarantee for the proposed iteration (and, by the paper's own motivation, the anticipated transfer to the discrete two-level RAS/GMRES setting) is unsupported as stated; the 'for any initial guess in H^1(Omega)' quantifier is not covered by any argument in the source.
issues.title: Convergence proof of the MS-GFEM iteration asserts an operator estimate that was never established
issues.why_classification: A contained, nontrivial reformulation (restricting the initial-data quantifier and rerunning the paper's own estimates on the appropriate error class) restores a recognizably comparable convergence theorem; the loss is limited to the 'any initial guess in H^1' quantifier, not to the method or its rate.

issues.failure_explanation: For the displayed velocity field, div b = d/dx1[20(x2-0.5)(1-(x1-0.5)^2) - 1.5(x1-0.5)] + d/dx2[20(x1-0.5)[1-(x2-0.5)^2] - 1.5(x2-0.5)] = -80(x1-0.5)(x2-0.5) - 3, which equals +17 at (x1,x2)=(0,1) and (1,0): the divergence is positive on part of the domain, contradicting 'has negative divergence'. (The reported grid Peclet number is also inconsistent: with h = 1/5120 and ||b||_{L^infty} about 10, Pe_h is about 2x10^3, not 3x10^3.) The indefiniteness conclusion only requires div b not vanishing identically, so the experiment itself is unaffected, but the stated mathematical property of the constructed field is false as written.
